subject: Three Colorado River states must take big water cuts as biggest US reservoirs plunge to record lows | CNN
posts:
Emergency cuts buy time for Lake Mead, but unequal state sacrifices expose deep cracks in century-old pacts.
Evidence: Shared survival, Unequal Lower Basin cuts, Comprehensive reform
#WaterCrisis #ColoradoRiver

The Interior Department frames the two-year plan as a vital pact stabilizing Lakes Mead and Powell, protecting regional power and drinking supplies.
Stated Judgement: (+0.81, +0.78) — Greater Good

Lower Basin states shoulder 100% of mandated cuts while Upper Basin states take zero, leaving the foundational 1922 allocation structural flaw unresolved.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.12, -0.18) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Awakening. Pragmatic stopgap averts immediate reservoir collapse but postpones systemic overhaul.
Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 2.15, z: 2)

- Lower Basin Mandates: COND (+0.18, -0.22) — Essential reductions, unequal state burden.
- Upper Basin Exemption: FAIL (-0.12, -0.15) — Defers needed systemic contributions.
Lake Mead and Powell fell to record lows, forcing a federal 2-year plan cutting water to Arizona, California, and Nevada through 2028.

The Bright Side:
Immediate emergency action prevents catastrophic reservoir dead-pool status and preserves power generation short-term.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing emergency rationing (WHAT) with permanent systemic balance (WHO). The 2-year band-aid leaves structural 1922 compact flaws untouched.

Social Physics Analysis:
Federal authorities averted immediate collapse by enforcing top-down rationing, yet asymmetrical burden-sharing risks inter-state legal conflict rather than durable consensus.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good. Tactical triage stabilizes water flow without fixing macro supply deficits.

The Unavoidable Truth: Short-term cuts prevent imminent reservoir depletion.
The Unavoidable Lie: A two-year Lower Basin sacrifice solves the regional structural crisis.

Physical limits always override legal treaties; realigning century-old water compacts to modern hydrological realities is inescapable.
